# situation: on issues, the step p, which has an id and whose shell: is
#   bash -x {0}, passes the title of the issue to git log, and the release
#   step writes the output tag of the step p into its script.
# reason: bash -x starts the script with the trace on, as set -x does, so
#   the trace prints the command with the title on the standard error,
#   where the runner reads ##[set-output name=NAME;] anywhere in a line as a
#   command that sets the output NAME of a step with an id; the title is
#   the attacker's.
# attack: the attacker opens an issue titled x ##[set-output
#   name=tag;]$(id).
# attack-run-behavior: the trace prints the git log command with the title,
#   the runner sets the output tag of the step to $(id), and the release
#   step writes the output into its script and runs id, with the token and
#   the secrets of the job.
on: workflow_call
permissions: {}
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: p
        shell: bash -x {0}
        env:
          TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        run: git log --grep "$TITLE" > log.txt
      - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
